prompt: Students should be allowed to choose academic courses or practical courses, e.g carpenters. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Although some people believe that students should focus on traditional academic subjects, I strongly agree that they should be free to choose between academic and practical courses, such as carpentry, according to their interests, abilities and future career goals.

To begin with, allowing students to choose their preferred courses can help them develop their strengths and maintain their interest in education. Every student has different abilities and interests, so it is unreasonable to expect everyone to follow the same academic path. For example, some students may have excellent mathematical or scientific abilities and therefore prefer subjects such as physics or computer science. In contrast, others may be more talented in practical activities and enjoy learning skills such as carpentry, plumbing or electrical work. When students study subjects that match their interests, they are more likely to remain motivated and perform well.

Another important reason is that practical courses can provide students with valuable skills and prepare them for employment. Not every student wants to attend university or work in an office, and skilled trades are essential to society. For instance, carpenters, electricians and plumbers are always needed to construct and maintain homes and other buildings. By learning these skills at school, students can gain practical experience and potentially enter the workforce soon after completing their education. This can also reduce the pressure on young people to obtain a university degree when it may not be necessary for their chosen career.

Furthermore, giving students a choice can create a more balanced education system. Academic and practical education should not be considered competitors; instead, they can complement each other. Students who receive opportunities to develop both theoretical knowledge and practical skills may become more confident and adaptable in their professional lives.

In conclusion, I completely agree that students should be allowed to choose between academic and practical courses. This approach can help them follow their interests, develop useful skills and prepare more effectively for their future careers.
